text:
eli: CI perf alert on PR #20684 — `microbench/kv_warmup_tail` shows ~22% tail latency regression compared to main. Observed in both x86 and aarch runners.

deploy-bot: CI job pr-20684/microbench-kv_warmup failed (exit 1) — see https://ci.company/teams/eng-runtime/20684/build/512.

ci-monitor: perf-diff summary:
- baseline (main): p99 = 12.3ms
- pr-20684: p99 = 15.0ms (+22%)
- test: `microbench/kv_warmup_tail` (seqlen=512, batch=1)

maria: @eli thanks for ping. This PR touched kernel_selector heuristics and the batching slot allocator — suspicious for warmup behavior. Any flamegraphs attached? :eyes:  

jae: quick flamegraph from the CI run (sanitized):
```
flamegraph: kernel_selector.py:select_kernel  48%
  -> batcher/slot_alloc.py:choose_slot  21%
  -> kvcache/prefetch.py:evict_and_prefetch  12%
  -> attention_kernels/gemm_path  7%
```
Noticing the selector spends more time scanning alternatives now.

eli: that matches local repro too. My profile showed an extra O(N) scan introduced in the new heuristic when seqlen distribution falls into the ambiguous bucket. It increases selector CPU on cold KV hits which delays the first tokens and spikes tail.

maria: can we bisect to the commit that introduced the scan? I started a quick git-bisect against main; earliest bad appears at commit `c3f8a1d` (kernel-selector: prefer lowest-cost even if warmup mismatch).

jae: confirmed `c3f8a1d` reproduces locally. Patch introduced here: https://git.company/r/redwood/runtime/commit/c3f8a1d

eli: proposal: revert the heuristics change for now and instead land a targeted fix that avoids scanning the whole kernel table when `kv_prefetch` is enabled. Revert PR would be smaller risk for rollout.

maria: +1 for revert as rollback path. Alternative is a hotfix that short-circuits the selector when `kv_hit_estimate > 0.6`. I sketched a patch:  
```diff
--- a/kernel_selector.py
+++ b/kernel_selector.py
@@
- for k in kernel_candidates:
-     score = full_cost_estimate(k)
+ for k in kernel_candidates:
+     if kv_prefetch and quick_kv_estimate(k) > 0.6:
+         score = cached_cost(k)
+     else:
+         score = full_cost_estimate(k)
```
This keeps most of the new logic but avoids the heavy scan for likely-warmup paths.

jae: can run a quick CI job with that patch applied to the PR branch. Eli — can you open a hotfix branch and trigger the perf job?

eli: creating branch `hotfix/pr-20684-kv-shortcircuit` and pushing now. Command I ran: `git checkout -b hotfix/pr-20684-kv-shortcircuit && git apply ../maria/kv-shortcircuit.patch && git push origin hotfix/pr-20684-kv-shortcircuit`

deploy-bot: Triggered job: pr-20684-hotfix/microbench-kv_warmup (build 513).

ci-monitor: early results (run 1): p99 = 12.6ms (baseline 12.3ms). Looks promising but need 5 runs to be confident.

maria: great. If repeated runs hold within noise, we can either cherry-pick the small short-circuit into the PR or revert `c3f8a1d` and reapply the heuristic with the short-circuit later.

jae: +1 for cherry-pick to minimize churn. Also want to add a unit perf test that asserts selector CPU budget < X ms for the warmup workload so this doesn't regress silently.

eli: agreed — I'll add a microbench asserting selector CPU < 3ms on a warmup trace. Planning to push tests after 5-run CI pass.

maria: sounds good. tagging @oncall to watch rollout if we merge the fix. :white_check_mark:

eli: tl;dr — root cause: heuristic introduced O(N) kernel scan on ambiguous seqlen buckets interacting badly with KV prefetch. Hotfix branch applied with short-circuit, CI shows initial recovery. Next: collect full CI runs, add selector CPU microtest, then merge hotfix/cherry-pick or revert original commit depending on stability.

jae: adding note to PR: "perf: short-circuit kernel selector for kv-prefetch warm paths; adds microbench for selector CPU."

ci-monitor: final aggregated runs (5 runs): p99 mean = 12.4ms, stdev = 0.2ms -> passes perf gate.

eli: merging hotfix patch into PR and will follow up with the microbench test. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
